thought_title: Deny the Flesh, Deny the Lord

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ὅν τινες ἀγνοοῦντες ἀρνοῦνται, μᾶλλον δὲ ἠρνήθησαν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ, ὄντες συνήγοροι τοῦ θανάτου μᾶλλον ἢ τῆς ἀληθείας: οὓς οὐκ ἔπεισαν αἱ προφητεῖαι οὐδὲ ὁ νόμος Μωύσεως, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ μέχρι νῦν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, οὐδὲ τὰ ἡμέτερα τῶν κατ’ ἄνδρα παθήματα. [2] καὶ γὰρ περὶ ἡμῶν τὸ αὐτὸ φρονοῦσιν. τί γάρ με ὠφελεῖ τις, εἰ ἐμὲ ἐπαινεῖ, τὸν δὲ κύριόν μου βλασφημεῖ, μὴ ὁμολογῶν αὐτὸν σαρκοφόρον; ὁ δὲ τοῦτο λέγων τελείως αὐτὸν ἀπήρνηται, ὢν νεκροφόρος. [3] τὰ δὲ ὀνόματα αὐτῶν, ὄντα ἄπιστα, οὐκ ἔδοξέν μοι ἐγγράψαι. ἀλλὰ μηδὲ γένοιτό μοι αὐτῶν μνημονεύειν, μέχρις οὗ μετανοήσωσιν εἰς τὸ πάθος, ὅ ἐστιν ἡμῶν ἀνάστασις.
pass_a_gloss: [1] Whom some deny out of ignorance, or rather they have been denied by him, being advocates of death rather than of the truth; whom the prophecies have not persuaded, nor the law of Moses, nor even the gospel up to now, nor our own sufferings, one by one. [2] For they think the same thing about us as well. For what does anyone benefit me if he praises me but blasphemes my Lord, not confessing that he bore flesh? And the one who says this has denied him completely, being one who bears a corpse. [3] Their names, since they are unbelieving, I have not thought fit to write down. Rather, may I not even remember them, until they repent and turn to the passion, which is our resurrection.
pass_b_english: Some deny him in ignorance. Better to say they have been denied by him. They plead the case for death rather than for the truth. The prophecies did not persuade them, nor the law of Moses. Even now the gospel has not, nor the sufferings each of us has borne.

For they think the same about us too. What good does anyone do me if he praises me but slanders my Lord, not confessing that he bore flesh? Whoever says this has denied him completely, and is a bearer of a corpse.
Their names are unbelieving names; I have not seen fit to write them down. May I not even remember them, until they repent and turn to the passion, which is our resurrection.

choices.english: bore flesh … is a bearer of a corpse
choices.why: Ignatius's wordplay: deny he bore flesh and you yourself bear a corpse. 'Bore/carries' keeps the echo.
rejected: possessed of a body … enveloped in death (ANF; loses the pun)

choices.why: Courtroom noun turned into a verb phrase a reader can say.

choices.english: repent and turn to the passion
choices.why: εἰς after the verb marks direction; 'turn to' supplies the English verb the preposition implies.
rejected: return to a true belief in Christ's passion (ANF; adds 'true belief')

choices.english: praises me but slanders my Lord
choices.why: βλασφημέω toward Christ; 'slanders' is the plain sense and keeps the contrast with 'praises'.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF adds '[truly]' and '[a true belief in]' and loses the flesh-bearer/corpse-bearer wordplay.

notes: Span: whole of Smyrnaeans 5 (sections 1, 2, 3); old ANF span covers the full chapter.
Pack topic: passion-resurrection. Same chapter English is shared by every excerpt id on this chapter.

Pack Greek reads 'ὁ δὲ τοῦτο λέγων' ('who says this'); other editions may read 'μὴ λέγων' ('who does not say this'). Sense is the same either way (denying the flesh = denying him), but a reviewer should check Lightfoot/Funk.
Possible echo of 2 Timothy 2:12 / Matthew 10:33 (denying and being denied); not marked inline.

Repair 2026-10-02 (round 2): optative μηδὲ γένοιτό μοι kept as a wish ('May I not even remember them'); 'refusing' and 'real' removed from the σαρκοφόρον clause; γάρ restored; 'rather than' kept for μᾶλλον ἤ.

review.notes: Locked Smyrnaeans 5 [1] matches both drafts clause for clause. Corrective passive 'μᾶλλον δὲ ἠρνήθησαν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ' is A's 'or rather they have been denied by him' and B's 'they have been denied by him'. Fourfold negation 'οὐκ ἔπεισαν αἱ προφητεῖαι οὐδὲ ὁ νόμος Μωύσεως, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ μέχρι νῦν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, οὐδὲ τὰ ἡμέτερα' stays negative in A ('have not persuaded, nor … nor even … nor') and B ('did not persuade them, nor the law of Moses. Even now the gospel has not, nor the sufferings'). Wish 'μηδὲ γένοιτό μοι αὐτῶν μνημονεύειν' is 'may I not even remember them' in both. 'σαρκοφόρον'/'νεκροφόρος' stay 'bore flesh'/'bearer of a corpse'; 'ὅ ἐστιν ἡμῶν ἀνάστασις' stays 'which is our resurrection'. No inline citation is present to mismatch. Title names the flesh-denial thought, not only the locus.

Pass A and Pass B accurately reflect the Greek source. No omissions, additions, or contradictions detected. All clauses preserved: ignorance-based denial, divine rejection, advocacy of death over truth, failure of prophecy, law, gospel, and sufferings to persuade; parallel thinking about the speaker; rhetorical question on praise vs. blasphemy; denial equated with corpse-bearing; refusal to name the unbelieving; wish to forget until repentance toward passion (resurrection). Inline scripture not present in source, so no citation check needed. Title reflects the theological thought (denial of flesh = denial of Lord). Notes disclose OCR damage handled and uncertain readings (variant in mss for 'ὁ δὲ τοῦτο λέγων'). Covered source paragraph: [1].
